# Modules and runtime classes

<!-- GENERATED by tools/docs_modules.py from boards/*.yaml, firmware/platformio.ini,
     tools/sdkconfig_fix.py and the firmware sources - do not edit by hand -->

ctrl32 runs on a **module** - the ESP32 part with its flash and PSRAM. A board is a
module with connectors around it, and the runtime binary is built **per module
class**, not per board: the pins, the display and the buses travel in the project
pack. This page says which modules exist, which runtime class each one gets, and
what that class can and cannot do - every number below is read from the sources
the binaries are built from.

## The rules - what, when, where, how

| What | When | How | Where in the code |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| WEBview viewers | a module **with PSRAM** | 2 at once (the declared product limit) | `webview_server.h` kMaxClients |
| WEBview viewers | a module **without PSRAM carrying a glass** | **1** viewer - the slim server; a second browser is refused at the handshake | `webview_server.cpp` add_client, `main.cpp` web_server_start (slim) |
| WEBview viewers | a module without PSRAM, headless | 2 | the headless app never asks for the slim server |
| WiFi buffers | every env without PSRAM | trimmed (static RX 4, dynamic RX/TX 8, mgmt 3/16): the AP attempt costs ~55 kB instead of ~75 | `sdkconfig_fix.py` WIFI_LEAN |
| WEBview server | every ESP module | started **after** CAN and the drives (logic > communication > graphics); skipped below 36 kB free with the reason in the diagnostic buffer | `main.cpp` web_server_start_pending |
| WEBview server | no PSRAM | slim: 3 sockets, no captive-portal DNS task - the phone types `192.168.4.1` | `main.cpp` web_server_start, `webview_server.cpp` |
| Fonts | every module | a built-in font is parsed on its FIRST use, the VLW stays in flash | `canvas.cpp` lazy_pre |
| Render bands | no PSRAM, an SPI glass | 1 band (the transfer is waited for before the next band) | `main.cpp` renderer.init, `Backend::wait_flush` |
| Render bands | everything else | 2 bands, the next one drawn while the previous goes out over DMA | `renderer.cpp` |
| TCP console `:3232` | no PSRAM carrying a glass | off (the serial console stays) | `upload_uart.cpp` start |
| MQTT TLS | ESP32-S3, ESP32-P4, STM32 | allowed (`mqtt.tls: true`, the firmware's CA bundle, buffers in PSRAM) | the editor and the pack build refuse it elsewhere |
| MQTT TLS | classic ESP32 / PICO | never | `proj_pack.cpp` - the desk refuses `mqtt.tls` off the S3/P4/STM32 |
| Trend traces | classic ESP32 / PICO | 4 in all | `main.cpp` g_trend_rec.set_limit(4) |
| Trend traces | ESP32-S3, ESP32-P4, Linux | 8 (4 per chart) | `visu_types.h` kLimitTrendSeries (from the schema) |
| Variables, alarms, blocks, axes | the LITE class: `variant_wroom32e` (ESP32 without PSRAM) | **128 variables, 32 alarms, 128 blocks, 1 axis** - the tables sized by the variable limit sit all over the runtime and cost 20 kB at 512; with the small tables the EVB with glass runs WiFi + CAN + WEBview with room to spare. The catalog says it (`limit_tags` / `limit_alarms` / `limit_blocks` / `limit_axes`), the desk refuses a bigger project, the runtime refuses a bigger pack and INFO says `cap=128,32,1` (the wall compares it with the catalog) | `platformio.ini` -DVISU_MAX_TAGS/-DVISU_MAX_ALARMS/-DVISU_MAX_AXES, `boards/*.yaml`, `proj_pack.cpp`, `main.cpp` |
| Project limits | a board with a display (type A) | 512 variables, 128 alarms, 32 screens, 64 widgets/screen, 512 blocks, 32 kB program, 8 kB instances | `visu_types.h` kLimit* (from the schema), the pack builder per target |
| Project limits | a headless board (type B) | the same, with 1024 blocks, 64 kB program, 24 kB instances | the pack builder per target |
| Project limits | Linux (type L) | 5120 variables, 1280 alarms, 320 screens, 256 widgets/screen, 5120 blocks, 320 kB program | `libvisu/CMakeLists` VISU_MAX_* |
| Modbus TCP | every ESP module | 4 connections at once | `main.cpp` - the Modbus TCP master |
| PSRAM on the S3 | octal dies (R8, R16V) | 80 MHz DDR, the standard | `sdkconfig_fix.py` PSRAM_S3_OCT |
| PSRAM on the S3 | quad dies (R2) | **not a slower mode - no PSRAM at all** on an octal-configured runtime; such a module has no runtime class | `sdkconfig_fix.py` PSRAM_S3_OCT groups |

## The chips - which get a runtime and why

A runtime needs **two cores** (the PLC cycle owns one, graphics and the network
share the other), **4 MB of flash** or more, **PSRAM** for a glass that carries
trends and assets, and an **Ethernet MAC** where the installation is wired. A
single-core chip gets no runtime; a chip that fails two of the four is not on
the list.

| Chip | Cores | GPIO (usable) | SRAM | PSRAM | Radio | Ethernet MAC | CAN | Display peripheral | Runtime |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| ESP32 (classic) | 2 x 240 MHz | 34 (~26) | 520 kB | quad, up to 8 MB | WiFi 4, BT | yes | 1 | SPI glass | yes - the LITE class without PSRAM, the standard class with |
| ESP32-PICO-V3-02 | 2 x 240 MHz | 34 (~26) | 520 kB | 2 MB in the package | WiFi 4, BT | yes | 1 | - | yes - headless |
| ESP32-S3 | 2 x 240 MHz | 45 (~33) | 512 kB | octal, up to 16 MB | WiFi 4, BLE 5 | no (SPI Ethernet) | 1 | i80, RGB | yes - the reference platform, four memory variants |
| ESP32-P4 | 2 x 400 MHz | 55 (~50) | 768 kB | up to 32 MB | through a companion chip | yes | 3 | MIPI DSI, RGB | yes |
| STM32F746 | 216 MHz M7 | up to 168 | 320 kB + 64 kB | external SDRAM | - | yes | 2 | LTDC | yes |
| STM32MP157 | 2 x 650 MHz A7 | ~170 | 512 MB | - | module | yes | 2 | LTDC, DSI | yes - the Linux runtime |
| Raspberry Pi CM4 / 4 / 5 | 4 x A72 / A76 | 28 | 1 - 8 GB | - | WiFi 5, BLE | yes | via SPI/USB | HDMI, DSI | yes - the Linux runtime |
| ESP32-S2, -C2, -C3, -C6, -C5, -C61, -H2 | 1 core | | | | | | | | no - single core |
| STM32H7, STM32F4, STM32G4 | M7 / M4 | | | | | | | | planned |

## Runtime classes - the binaries

One binary per class; a catalog board names its class, a bare module names it
too. The sdkconfig groups are the build's memory facts; the rules above decide
the rest at run time from what the board has.

## The modules

Grouped by chip. *Runtime class* is the binary the editor flashes for the module;
a module whose flash and PSRAM combination has no class yet cannot be a target's
runtime until that class exists (spec 022 phase 4) - the editor's Upload offers
nothing for it, deliberately. The boards column lists the catalog boards built on
that class.

The measurement behind the no-PSRAM rules (Olimex ESP32-EVB with the
2.8" module, CAN and the i550 program): 122.6 kB internal RAM after the model,
114.3 kB after the display (one band), 101.6 kB at the network stage, 46.1 kB
after the WiFi access point came up, 44.8 kB after CAN, 20.8 kB after the WEBview
server, ~12 kB free at run time - one viewer, at the edge. A module with PSRAM
needs none of the diet.
